analysis.title: GS flow and positioning observations
key_insights: Overnight US rebound carried into the tech tape: Hynix +5%, Samsung +4%, KOSPI +3%. The desk asks whether this is an oversold bounce in QQQ or the start of a more sustainable move. It notes that the week before major political events, with this much risk premium already priced, tends to be constructive.

Gulf diplomacy is the main energy focus. Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani delegations are in Tehran and Qatar is mediating. Nothing substantive has emerged, and the desk sees low odds of a breakthrough. If there is no progress by Thursday morning, escalation could resume into the weekend. Oil has come off Friday's escalatory highs.

HSBC fell 5.6% in Hong Kong. Deposit competition in the UK and Hong Kong is compressing net interest income (NII). The desk flags the same risk for European banks, along with the background threat of agentic capital allocation.

AI credit is the most important thing to watch. Spreads came off Friday's wides, but the desk says the cost of capital has risen materially and is changing the economics of the AI complex. Sustained relief in credit would be a powerful catalyst. The desk also raises the possibility that heavy spending eventually causes compute oversupply into 2027/28, lower returns and lower multiples, and calls this unclear.

AI earnings are strong. Celestica rose about 17% after hours, beat, and guided to $40bn of 2027 revenue (+90% YoY) with 2028 demand indications even stronger. Cadence beat and raised with $8.2bn of backlog. Rambus beat but slipped after the close. The desk says demand is not the problem and the debate is how to discount future cash flows given supply, competition and financing uncertainty.
Neoclouds were under pressure after Elon's comments on financing and consolidation.

Front-end rates have stabilized, which the desk calls good for risk. Energy is too high for comfort but is more likely to produce chop than a sustained selloff absent escalation. Credit is still flashing yellow to red relative to equities, and the desk wants credit to calm down as a catalyst for a broader rally.

For the hyperscaler earnings and the Fed this week the desk watches four things: capex (flat or up is fine, down would be disastrous for picks and shovels), backlog conversion into revenue, free cash flow conversion in the out quarters, and financing (equity versus debt for the next leg).

Flows were somewhat more supportive. After weeks as net sellers of tech, the desk saw client demand on the other side, at least in Europe. The modal view is that markets chop until next week's political events clear.

US close: S&P +70bps at 7,676 with a $3.5bn market-on-close imbalance to sell. NDX +109bps at 29,273, R2K +42bps at 2,787, Dow +28bps at 52,361. Volume was 16.630bn shares against a year-to-date daily average of 18.513bn. The bounce was broad, with signs of AI stabilization.

US sales trading says the bounces of the last two weeks, including today, are mostly driven by the end of high-velocity supply, with little sign of offense in AI and tech. Desk activity was muted and activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale.

Brazil's EWZ traded -20%, its worst session outside Covid (-23%), after Lula won the presidential race despite a first-round deficit, defying prediction market expectations. The desk says this is only the third presidential election Polymarket has gotten wrong.

Skew collapsed out of the weekend and spot vol compressed with the rally. NDX vol underperformed despite the tech-led outperformance, which highlights the steep NDX/S&P vol spread. Tomorrow's S&P implied move priced at 50bps and the desk expects daily straddles to stay in that range.

The desk favors QQQ short-dated call spreads to capture a potential positioning squeeze through earnings and election catalysts, specifically the QQQ 13Nov 735/755 call spread at just under 5x gross payout.
AMZN upside stands out ahead of Thursday's earnings because the stock is over 12% off its August highs. The desk prefers capped upside structures out to December.
The week has central bank decisions (FOMC, BOC, ECB, BOJ) and earnings from 44% of S&P market cap, led by MSFT, GOOG, AMZN and INTC.
